title: The Perfect Will Again
premise: Rafael Halloran, the coroner of Ash Hollow, has spent years quietly correcting the record on deaths the police mislabeled as accidents. When a stranger's body is found dressed in clothes stolen from Rafael's own closet, staged to look like Rafael themselves, it becomes clear someone has studied every unsolved case file — including the three deaths Rafael solved in secret. With Detective Imogen Voss torn between trusting Rafael and suspecting them, the two form an uneasy alliance to bait a killer who seems to know their moves before they make them. At the town's anniversary dinner, where the whole of Ash Hollow gathers under one roof, Rafael springs a trap built on a falsified case file, unmasking the killer as the retired archivist who kept the town's records — and whose own family was destroyed by a death Rafael once reclassified.
about_author: Noor Thornbury is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper reporter who spent a decade covering coroner's inquests and county court dockets. They write mysteries about people who keep their towns' secrets and the cost of finally telling the truth.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Rafael Halloran's POV. A quiet autumn morning in Ash Hollow: Rafael walks the cemetery they know intimately, reflecting on the three deaths they quietly proved were murders while police filed them as accidents. The beat is melancholy competence — a keeper of truths no one asked for — ending when a jogger screams near the old mill road.

chapters.title: The Wrong Clothes
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The body at the mill road wears Rafael's own missing cardigan, scarf, and boots, staged with uncanny precision down to a replicated autopsy tag. Detective Imogen Voss arrives, and her first question — 'Where were you last night?' — lands like a betrayal. The emotional beat is violation: the killer hasn't just killed, they've impersonated Rafael.

chapters.title: What the File Doesn't Say
chapters.summary: Imogen's POV. Imogen reviews the official case files and finds them disturbingly complete — complete in ways only someone with archive access could manage. She notices the victim's fingerprints match a drifter reported missing two towns over, meaning the staging was planned for weeks. Her beat is suspicion warring with instinct: everything points at Rafael, yet nothing fits.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Ash Hollow prepares its sesquicentennial dinner, a tradition Rafael dreads because the whole town attends — including everyone connected to the old cases. A threatening note arrives in Rafael's handwriting, which Rafael never wrote. The beat is mounting dread: the killer isn't hiding anymore; they're announcing themselves inside Rafael's own life.

chapters.title: Three Accidents, Revisited
chapters.summary: Dual POV, alternating Rafael and Imogen. They compare notes for the first time, walking through the three deaths Rafael secretly solved: a fall, a drowning, a fire. Each file shows signs of being read, annotated, and returned. The emotional beat is reluctant partnership — two guarded people realizing the killer knows both of them better than they know each other.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Daughter
chapters.summary: Imogen's POV. Following the paper trail, Imogen finds that all four victims connect to records handled by Wendell Marsh, the town's retired archivist, whose daughter died twenty years ago in a death ruled accidental — a ruling Rafael quietly overturned in his private notes but never made public. The beat is cold horror: Rafael's secret justice may have lit this fuse.

chapters.title: Confession at the Diner
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael confronts what their hidden corrections cost: Marsh's daughter's death was tied to a cover-up Rafael exposed to himself but never to the law, leaving the guilty unpunished and grief unacknowledged. When Marsh appears at the diner, calm and courteous, he quotes Rafael's own private notes back to him verbatim. The beat is guilt curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Baiting the Hook
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Rafael proposes a dangerous plan: plant a falsified case file claiming new evidence about Marsh's daughter will be revealed at the anniversary dinner, forcing Marsh to act. Imogen risks her career by agreeing off the books. The beat is resolve — loyalty to the dead outweighing loyalty to procedure, and each trusting the other with their career and life.

chapters.title: A Toast to Ash Hollow
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs through the dinner. As the mayor raises the anniversary toast, Marsh slips away toward the records room where the planted file waits — and where Rafael, not an empty office, sits waiting. Marsh attacks; Imogen intervenes; in the struggle Marsh confesses to all four killings, each staged as penance for the town that buried his daughter's truth. The beat is explosive climax.

chapters.title: The Record, Corrected
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, weeks later. Marsh awaits trial; the daughter's case is officially reopened, her name spoken aloud at a small graveside gathering attended by unlikely found family — Imogen, the victims' kin, the town. Rafael adds a fourth stone to their private mental map of graves, then lets the secret ledger go. The beat is bittersweet peace: justice served outside the law, truth finally on the record.
